# 四書纂疏

## Authors / Editors
- 趙順孫 (宋朝) 撰

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 28-*juàn* sub-commentary on Zhū Xī's *Sìshū jízhù*, gathering the supplementary discussions of thirteen named Zhū Xī disciples and second-generation transmitters and arranging them by *Sìshū* passage. The work is the late-Sòng counterpart to Yuán-period *jíshì* 集釋 / *zuǎnshū* 纂疏 compilations, and one of the principal *Sìshū* sub-commentaries of the post-Sòng era.

**Abstract**

The *Sìshū zuǎnshū* is the most thorough surviving compilation of post-Zhū-Xī *Sìshū* sub-commentary. The thirteen named contributors include all the major early-13th-century Zhū Xī transmitters: Huáng Gàn (Zhū Xī's son-in-law and chief intellectual heir); Chén Chún (the systematiser of *Lǐxué* terms in the *Běixī zìyì* 北溪字義); Cài Yuān, Cài Shěn (the *Shū*-jiā 蔡 family, [KR1b0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0019) etc., here through Cài Mó's *Mèngzǐ jíshū* [KR1h0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0025)); Yè Wèidào, Hú Yǒng, Chén Zhí, Pān Bǐng, Huáng Shìyì (compiler of the most authoritative version of the *Yǔlèi*); Zhēn Déxiù ([KR1h0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0024)); plus Fǔ Guǎng, Chén Kǒngshuò.

Through these thirteen, Zhào Shùnsūn provides a comprehensive survey of orthodox Cheng-Zhu *Sìshū* commentary as it stood by the mid-13th century — a useful "encyclopedia" of Zhū Xī school readings before the disruptions of the Sòng-Yuán transition. As the Sìkù tíyào notes, the absence of Zhēn Déxiù's *Sìshū jíbiān* ([KR1h0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0024)) from the citation-list — though Zhēn Déxiù's other works are cited extensively — is explained by the fact that the *Jíbiān* was first cut for print at the very end of the Sòng (as the Sìkù tíyào at [KR1h0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0024) confirms), too late for Zhào Shùnsūn to have seen it.

The Sìkù editors' defence against the charge of *rǒnglàn* (verbosity) is methodologically interesting: they invoke the standard pre-Sòng distinction between *zhù*-style brevity and *shū*-style fullness, and argue that *zuǎnshū* is a self-conscious imitation of Kǒng Yǐngdá and Jiǎ Gōngyàn — i.e. of Táng-period *zhèngyì* practice. By this standard, the work is doing exactly what it sets out to do.

The textual history is well-recorded; the work was first cut for print in the final years of the Sòng (per the Sìkù tíyào's reference to Zhēn Déxiù's *Jíbiān*); the WYG transmits a Yuán-period reprint.
